title: Shige Sushi Counter
premise: A long itamae drama at the hinoki counter. Xiaolin and Xiaoshuang are easily confused by looks; the bluefin tuna yanagiba goes intact_edge→chipped_edge→resharpened; after the delivery bicycle is wrecked it must be avoided; soba cups / tea cups / wind chimes count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_on_duty: Itamae Amao around fifty, white jacket, navy apron, adhesive bandage on the wrist, steady knife work.
states.weary_injured: The same Amao: apron torn, fingers wrapped in thick gauze, still insisting on walking, eyes heavier.
states.retired_exit: Amao has left the counter; only his navy apron and white jacket remain—he himself no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Apprentice Xiaolin of fourteen or fifteen, indigo headscarf, short white jacket, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Xiaolin in his twenties, still in indigo headscarf, upright and steady.

states.intact_edge: A willow-blade bluefin tuna yanagiba, long bright blade, hackberry wood handle carved with the character Shige.
states.chipped_edge: The same willow blade with a nick missing a small chip; fish fibers tug when cutting.
states.resharpened: After resharpening the willow-blade nick is filled, edge keen again, old Shige still on the handle.

states.intact: A waterproof-covered prep ledger recording fish species, purchase price, and yield rate.
states.soy_stained: The same prep ledger soaked through with soy sauce, cover sticky, writing bled.

states.intact: A dark-green delivery bicycle with a warmer box strapped to the basket, white Shige Sushi lettering on the frame.
states.rear_ended_wrecked: After a truck rear-ends it, the delivery bicycle wheels twist and the frame snaps—wreckage.

states.young_rival: Youth Xiaoshuang whose face closely matches Xiaolin's, cream neckerchief, same short white jacket, swaggering look.
states.disguised_return: After a change of look Xiaoshuang still wears the cream neckerchief; expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Amao lifts the noren into the sushi counter and first wipes the bluefin tuna yanagiba.
A row of five tea cups hangs on wooden pegs above the counter; Amao polishes each one.
Two wind chimes hang beside the noren; Amao reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Amao circles the hinoki top checking the cold-case temperature.
Amao looks through the glass toward street lamps dimming toward the market.
The willow blade catches lamplight; Amao gently tests the edge.
Amao sits on the small stool inside the counter for a brief rest.
Amao opens the prep ledger and notes today's tuna yield rate.
Amao sketches a fat-line distribution chart in the prep ledger.
Amao closes the prep ledger and returns it to the counter drawer.
The willow blade flashes by the cutting board; Amao nods.
Amao wipes water beads from the ledger cover with a dry cloth.
In the walk-in fridge aisle at dawn, Amao greets young Xiaolin pushing the delivery bicycle.
Xiaolin steadies the bicycle and snaps the warmer box shut.
Amao points to three soba cups at the counter corner and teaches Xiaolin guest cup positions.
Xiaolin crouches in the cold aisle watching condensate drip from the pipes.
Amao explains hand warmth for nigiri; Xiaolin nods earnestly.
Xiaolin looks back at the dark-green delivery bicycle, eyes full of tension.
Amao has Xiaolin first practice rolling vinegar-rice balls.
In the noisy market middleman aisle, Xiaoshuang in a cream neckerchief looks up from behind foam boxes.

segments.action: In rainy season Amao stands damp cutting boards upright to dry at the sushi counter.
Amao pushes the willow-blade edge on a whetstone.
At dawn Amao checks tuna price sheets at the market.
Amao hangs a raincoat on the back door and listens to the crushed-ice truck pass.
In high summer Amao lowers the cold-case temperature one degree.
Amao checks vinegar-rice acidity, tasting with the tip of his tongue.
When autumn wind rises Amao takes in the sidewalk menu board.
Amao trials new fish-species codes on a blank prep-ledger page.
On a frost night Amao lights a small lamp and checks flashlight charge.
Amao wraps rice sacks in a blanket against night damp.
On a heavy-snow day Amao sweeps thin snow from the noren-entrance stone steps.
Amao blows on his hands and tightens the warmer-box latch.
At spring start Amao clears fish scales from the back-door drain.
Amao scalds and washes the five tea cups one by one.
Amao posts a new today's specials sheet on the counter wall.
Around Dragon Boat Festival Amao smokes the rice store with mugwort against insects.
Amao retraces the blue patterns on the soba cups.
Amao paces the cold aisle alone, silently memorizing guest allergies.
After rain Amao opens the back door and listens to eave water drip into an iron bucket.
Amao swaps worn towels for new ones.
Another dusk Amao sits by the willow blade listening to the radio.
Amao rises at night to defrost the cold case.
Amao seals newly arrived nori jars for storage.
Amao wipes the Shige Sushi lettering at the noren entrance.
Amao checks the delivery bicycle basket binding rope.
Amao crosses out out-of-season fish on the menu.
Amao wrings soy-stained rags dry and hangs them.
On a full-moon night Amao looks out toward the market; crushed ice flashes.
Amao arranges the wooden pegs so tea-cup mouths face the same way.
Amao writes the new season's prep notes on the ledger flyleaf.
Amao polishes the two wind chimes bright.
Amao listens to market unloading and keeps chopping scallions.
Amao glues a cracked rice paddle.
Amao piles dishes to wash in the counter corner.
Amao latches the back door tight so night cats cannot enter.
Another Qingming Amao sets a nandina sprig at the noren entrance.
Amao rolls the price list into a tube and binds it with a rubber band.
Amao tests the wind chimes' clear ring.
Amao sits mute at the counter listening long to the fridge compressor hum.
Amao cuts worn indigo cloth into rag stock.
Amao wets the whetstone surface, ready to sharpen at dawn.
Amao shreds ginger into fine strands and portions them into small dishes.
At daybreak Amao patrols the walk-in fridge aisle; the delivery bicycle sits by the back door.
Amao crouches to check the bicycle tires.
Amao walks to the counter corner; those three soba cups still stack in place.
A white delivery scooter passes the back door, slim body—not the Shige Sushi bicycle.
Amao stands in the cold aisle logging the cold-case temperature curve.
Amao hangs a wet apron on the aisle wooden rack.
Amao pats ice crumbs from his sleeve and looks back at the counter lights.
After Grain Rain Amao teaches a new apprentice to judge fish-eye freshness in the cold aisle.
Amao re-starches the sun-dried apron.
In summer heat Amao lays a wet cloth on the rice tub to cool it.
Amao checks the bicycle rear basket and swaps a damp warmer pad for a new one.
On an autumn night Amao mends loose prep-ledger pages under a small lamp.
Amao rotates the five tea cups through disinfection.
At first snow Amao sweeps a narrow path at the noren entrance.
Amao reseals spare nori.
Amao listens to the wind chimes and keeps correcting orders.
Amao opens the back door so a draft carries fish-damp air away.
Amao hangs a rain canvas in the doorway.
Amao stores a chipped old blade in a tin box.
At night Amao dreams of fish gone bad and wakes to note it in the ledger.
Amao rinses the soba cups with clear water.
Amao wipes and reposts today's specials.
Amao pulls weeds from the back-door stone seams.
Amao hangs the tea cups back on pegs; number slips have faded a little.
Before lights-out Amao takes one last look at the willow-blade edge.
Amao folds an indigo headscarf an apprentice left on the counter.
Amao hears the market closing horn and rises to lock up.
Amao dries gloves by charcoal fire.
Amao shifts the wind chimes aside to show the freshly washed noren.
Amao air-dries the temperature probe.
Amao draws a yield-rate comparison at the ledger end.
Amao silently recites tomorrow's fish list and steps out the noren entrance.
Amao pushes the bicycle to the wall foot, freeing the back-door passage.
Amao hears a distant tram and blows out the small lamp.
Another rainy night Amao alone keeps the counter until dawn.
Amao grinds newly arrived wasabi root into paste.
Amao writes guests' usual nigiri styles on a small blackboard.
On a storm night a truck loses control in the back alley; the crash reaches the counter.
In the jolt the cutting board leaps hard.
A crisp crack—a nick bursts from the bluefin tuna yanagiba edge.
